documents.title: What Is Coral Bleaching?

evidence.text: microscopic algae called zooxanthellae that live in their tissues
questions: What is the name of the microscopic algae living in coral tissue?

evidence.text: These algae are the coral’s primary food source and give them their color.
questions: What two things do the resident algae provide to healthy coral?

evidence.text: Increased ocean temperature caused by climate change is the leading cause of coral bleaching.
questions: What leading cause of bleaching does the infographic identify?

evidence.text: Storm generated precipitation can rapidly dilute ocean water and runoff can carry pollutants — these can bleach near-shore corals.
questions: What effect of storm-generated precipitation can bleach corals close to shore?

evidence.text: When temperatures are high, high solar irradiance contributes to bleaching in shallow-water corals.
questions: How can strong sunlight affect shallow-water corals when temperatures are high?

evidence.text: Exposure to the air during extreme low tides can cause bleaching in shallow corals.
questions: What happens to shallow corals exposed to air during unusually low tides?

missing_detail_questions: How many days does a bleached coral take to recover?
